# Feature: Proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1)

**STATUS: DEFERRED — implementation delayed until client-side compaction
results are available.** Client-side compaction machinery is now in place in
ContextHub (Compact-and-Continue WL-0MR269PDV00970YP, auto-continue
WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O; gate-response wiring WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6). Per
operator decision (2026-08-28), server-side compaction must not be
implemented until results from the client-side effort are reviewed; this
item is parked (status `blocked`) pending that review.

Implementation of the F4 recommendation (LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW,
`docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`) within the two-tier scheme of
LP-0MTCW79RR000LFMJ. The proxy compacts the session at **prompt-assembly
time** when estimated tokens exceed the trigger — no round trip, no
client-side coordination.

## Behavior (both modes — Strategy C, summarize-first)

Per operator decision (2026-08-28), serve-side compaction uses the hybrid
Strategy C in **both** fast and cheap modes, with the **first prompt always
retained verbatim**.

### Retention invariant (fast AND cheap)

The compacted prompt MUST always contain, unchanged:

1. the system prompt;
2. the **very first user prompt** (the original task statement/setup, which
   carries essential instructions);
3. the most recent turns within budget.

Everything between the first prompt and the recent window is folded into a
summary injected at the top of the prompt (below the retained first prompt).

### Fast mode — Strategy C

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 58,300` (= 0.70 × per-slot clamp 83,285).
  Fires before the existing `context_pressure_warn_ratio` (0.8 × 83,285 =
  66.6K) so compaction is proactive, not reactive.
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 38,000 tokens (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`,
  fast profile): retain system prompt + first prompt + recent turns; fold
  the rest into a summary.
- **Backstop:** only if the session still exceeds budget after summarizing,
  drop oldest non-first turns (whole turns, never splittable, never the
  system prompt or first prompt), logged.
- **Automatic** on breach.

### Cheap mode — Strategy C (hybrid)

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 43,000` (= 0.70 × static clamp 61,440).
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 30,000 tokens: same retention invariant +
  summary of the middle.
- **Non-compactable** (summarizer unavailable, or still over budget after
  compaction): route remote with guidance — never silent remote fallback,
  never near-full-slot local prefill (LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D AC4).
- **Automatic** on breach.

## Implementation approach

- **Trigger hook:** reuse the existing `context_pressure` machinery in
  `proxy/provider.py` (`context_pressure_ratio` / `should_warn_context_pressure`,
  LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC). Add a configurable compaction trigger ratio
  (default 0.70), distinct from the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio (unchanged).
- **Compaction at prompt assembly:** session history is a message list;
  summarization/truncation operates on it before dispatch. Composes with
  slot save/restore (compacted prompts restore cleanly under the
  persistence cap).
- **Summarizer:** short proxy-generated summary (cheap local call) injected
  at the top of the prompt; with summarizer-unavailable fallback to the
  truncate backstop.
- **Logging:** every compaction event logs session, before/after estimated
  tokens, turns summarized, turns dropped, summary length — traceability
  for quality regressions (F3 §7). Nothing is silent.
- **Rollout phases:**
  1. **Warn-only dry-run** — advisory (would-summarize/would-drop) log +
     stats for 48h; validate churn (< 1 compaction/session/hour) against
     F1/F2 distributions; **no dispatch behavior change**.
  2. **Enforcement** — gated on the quality experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ)
     passing its bar AND operator review of client-side compaction results.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 Both modes: compacted prompt retains system prompt + very first user
  prompt verbatim + recent turns; middleware summarized (never silently
  dropped).
- AC2 Fast: est > 58,300 → compacted to ≤ 38K; backstop drop only for
  non-summarizable middle turns, logged, never system/first prompt.
- AC3 Cheap: est > 43,000 → compacted to ≤ 30K; non-compactable → remote
  with guidance (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local dispatch).
- AC4 Trigger routed through `context_pressure` machinery; compaction
  trigger ratio 0.70 configurable; 0.8 warn ratio behavior unchanged.
- AC5 All compaction events logged (session, before/after est tokens, turns
  summarized, turns dropped, summary length).
- AC6 Warn-only dry-run phase produces advisory logs + churn stats with
  zero dispatch changes; dry-run threshold validation recorded.
- AC7 Unit tests: retention invariant (first prompt kept), summary path,
  truncate backstop boundaries, turn-split prohibition, non-compactable
  routing, warn-only mode. Full suite green.
- AC8 Enforcement only after experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ) passes its
  bar AND client-side compaction review (ContextHub WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6) is
  complete; no behavior change in warn-only phase.

## Interaction analysis (from F4 §5)

- **Slot save/restore:** summary + recent turns are byte-stable → clean
  restores under the persistence cap.
- **Hard-routing-cap companion (Tier 2, LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S):** cap at
  70K/61.4K is the final bypass guard; compaction trigger fires below it so
  sessions rarely reach the cap.
- **KV-cache quantization (LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC):** additive — compaction
  shrinks context length, q8_0 shrinks bytes/token; both raise decode
  headroom.

## Out of scope

- Client-side compaction UX (ContextHub owns it; see WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6).
- 150K–480K HTTP-400 cluster (LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K).
- Changing the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio.

## Dependencies

- Depends on LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ (quality experiment) for the enforcement
  go/no-go.
- **Blocked pending:** client-side compaction results (ContextHub
  WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6 and completed compact-and-continue machinery) —
  operator decision 2026-08-28 to delay server-side until those are
  reviewed.
- Complementary to LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (Tier 2 hard cap + cheap gate).

The slot_schedule removal (LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V) removes the time-based slot schedule from proxy/config.yaml, config-fast.yaml, config-cheap.yaml.

Required work (in the skill directory, per .pi boundary this item must be explicitly authorized):
- Derive per-mode slot counts from the mode profiles' static session_slot_pool_size (fast 3 / cheap 2) instead of schedule entries.
- Replace ctx_by_time semantics with the profiles' static local_model_ctx_size.
- Update recommendations text that references 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule'.
- Update skill tests/fixtures accordingly.

## Goal

Increase **genuine** local-model busy time (the share of wall-clock time at least one local slot is actively generating) by raising **local capture** — the share of total demand that reaches a local slot — without degrading client latency or error rates.

Baseline from the 24h proxy-usage report (2026-10-13 14:39 → 2026-10-14 14:39):

| Quantity | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Total compute (slot-time) | 12h 07m = **50.4%** of window | Ceiling for busy% at today's local volume |
| Actual busy | 8h 45m = **36.5%** | Utilisation achieved |
| Packing loss | 13.9 pts | Lost to concurrency >1 (avg 1.38) |
| Capture loss | local 1,454 / 10,017 = **14.5%** | 85.5% of demand never reached a slot |

Packing alone can add at most ~14 points (36.5 → ~50). Getting materially above 50% requires **capture** — routing more of the 85.5% remote traffic to local, which raises the compute ceiling itself. **Capture is therefore the priority.**

## Why capture is lost

Fallback split (8,100 events):

| Fallback reason | Share | Reaches a slot? |
|---|---|---|
| `large_context_bypass` | 46.6% (99.9% fast) | **No** — router decides before slot check |
| `context_too_large` | 27.2% (71% cheap) | **No** |
| `fallback_after_queue` | 23.1% | **Yes** — slot check, then queue timeout/depth |
| `local_lease_active` | 1.0% | **Yes** — slot held by idle lease |

**~74% of fallbacks are decided upstream of the slot pool.**

## The two thresholds (how the gate actually works)

Source: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_effective_large_context_thresholds()`, `_should_skip_local()`, `effective_large_context_economic_ceiling()`.

The gate has **three** terms, resolved as:

```
effective_warm = min(physical per-slot clamp, economic ceiling, hard routing cap)
physical       = local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096        (output headroom)
economic       = min(round(ratio x local_model_ctx_size), absolute warm_cache_threshold)
```

- **`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`** (COLD) — an **economic new-token** threshold, *not scalable, not clamped*. It is the `(cold, warm]` band's lower edge. A request whose **new (uncached) tokens** exceed COLD is skipped with reason `large_context_bypass` — *unless* the mode sets `local_large_context_economic_bypass_serves_local: true` (cheap does; fast does not). Because `new_tokens = int(est x (1 - cached_ratio))`, a restarted or cold session (cached_ratio ≈ 0) triggers at a **full re-prefill cost**, not a marginal one.
- **`local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio`** (WARM, economic term) — scales linearly with `local_model_ctx_size`, capped by the absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`. **It is a ceiling for total context**: a request whose total estimate exceeds it is skipped with reason `context_too_large`.
- The terms **interact**: the economic ceiling only bites when it is *below* the physical per-slot clamp. Today fast runs **1 slot**, so physical = 258,048 and economic = 100,000 → economic dominates. Cheap runs **3 slots**, so physical = 83,285 → physical dominates.

## Current profile (verified, 2026-10-14)

| Mode | Slots | Physical clamp | Economic ceiling | Effective warm | Cold | `economic_bypass_serves_local` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fast | 1 | 258,048 | min(100,008, 100,000) = 100,000 | **100,000** | **38,000** | false |
| cheap | 3 | 83,285 | min(100,008, 100,000) = 100,000 | **83,285** | **42,000** | true |

Modelled against the config, verified numerically.

## Worked examples

Each row: one session, `(cached_ratio, estimated_tokens)` from the log, run through `_should_skip_local` under the stated config.

### Example 1 — the cold threshold is the binding fast-mode constraint

Config: fast, COLD=38,000, WARM=100,000. `est = 60,000`, `cached_ratio = 0.0` (cold session, e.g. post-restart or new prefix).
`new = int(60,000 x 1.0) = 60,000` > COLD 38,000 → **`large_context_bypass`**. `60,000 < WARM` 100,000, so `context_too_large` never fires.
**Raise COLD 38,000 → 55,000:** `60,000 > 55,000` → still bypasses. **Raise COLD → 65,000:** `60,000 <= 65,000` → **routed local.** This session's ~30.7s stream (report avg) now contributes busy time.

### Example 2 — same session count, three cold-ratio outcomes

Config: fast, WARM=100,000, `est = 60,000`.
- `cached_ratio = 0.00` → `new = 60,000` > 38,000 → **`large_context_bypass`**
- `cached_ratio = 0.70` → `new = 18,000` <= 38,000 → **routed local**
- `cached_ratio = 0.85` → `new = 9,000` <= 38,000 → **routed local**

The **same session at the same context size** flips on cache warmth alone. This is why cold restarts after the 01:00/10:00 mode switches concentrate `large_context_bypass` — every session is a full re-prefill.

### Example 3 — the two thresholds bite at different sizes

Config: fast, COLD=38,000, WARM=100,000. `cached_ratio = 0.0` (worst case).
- `est = 30,000` → `new = 30,000` <= 38,000 → **local**
- `est = 60,000` → `new = 60,000` > 38,000; `60,000 < 100,000` → **`large_context_bypass`**
- `est = 130,000` → `130,000 > 100,000` → **`context_too_large`** (Check 1 fires before the cold check)

So COLD governs the **38k–100k** range (46.6% of fallbacks) and WARM governs **>100k** (the cheap-dominated 27.2%).

### Example 4 — raising the ratio alone does NOTHING until the absolute warm cap moves

Config: fast, `local_model_ctx_size = 262,144`, absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold = 100,000`.
- `ratio 0.3815` → `round(0.3815 x 262,144) = 100,008`, `min(100,008, 100,000)` = **100,000**
- `ratio 0.45` → `round(0.45 x 262,144) = 117,965`, `min(117,965, 100,000)` = **100,000 ← unchanged**
- `ratio 0.55` → `round(0.55 x 262,144) = 144,179`, `min(144,179, 100,000)` = **100,000 ← unchanged**

**The absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 100000` dominates the ratio.** Any ratio-only change is inert. To raise fast warm to ~144k you must set the ratio to ~0.55 **and** raise the absolute warm cap to >= 144,179. This corrects the framing in the originating analysis (which cited "0.3815 → 0.55 lifts fast warm to ~144k" without noting the absolute cap).

### Example 5 — combined fast raise, verified

Config: fast, COLD 38,000 → 55,000 **and** WARM 100,000 → 144,179 (ratio 0.55).
- `est = 150,000`, `ratio = 0.0` → `new = 150,000` > 55,000, but `150,000 > 144,179` → **`context_too_large`** (hard cap still protects)
- `est = 140,000`, `ratio = 0.0` → `new = 140,000` > 55,000, `140,000 <= 144,179` → **`large_context_bypass`** (cold check still protects)
- `est = 140,000`, `ratio = 0.95` → `new = 7,000` <= 55,000 → **routed local**
- `est = 50,000`, `ratio = 0.0` → `new = 50,000` <= 55,000 → **routed local** (was bypassed at 38,000 cold)

### Example 6 — a 200k context is unreachable in fast mode

`est = 200,000`. Fast true ceiling = **100,000** (economic). `context_too_large` regardless of cache — even at `cached_ratio = 0.99` (`new = 2,000`). Even lifting warm to 144,179 leaves this remote; only cheap (effective warm 83,285... *lower*) or a deeper warm raise reaches it.

### Example 7 — COLD vs the physical clamp (cheap's failure mode)

Cheap: slots=3, physical=83,285, `cached_ratio=0.0`, COLD=42,000.
- `est = 50,000` → `new = 50,000` > 42,000, but `economic_bypass_serves_local: true` → **served locally** (queues, does not fall back)
- `est = 90,000` → `90,000 > 83,285` → **`context_too_large`** (0.0% fast, 100.0% cheap skip share)

**Reduce cheap slots 3 → 2:** physical becomes `262,144//2 - 4,096 = 126,976` → WARM rises to `min(100,000, 126,976) = 100,000` (**only +16,715**, because the absolute 100,000 now binds instead of the physical clamp), so cheap `context_too_large` shrinks modestly; the cost is one slot of concurrency. To get the full 126,976 the absolute warm cap would also need raising.

### Example 8 — the end-to-end gate today

Fast path, in code order:
1. COLD disabled (`cold <= 0`) → route local. *(not our case)*
2. `est > WARM(100,000)` → `context_too_large`
3. `est <= COLD(38,000)` → route local
4. `new = int(est x (1 - ratio))`; `new <= 38,000` → route local
5. else → `large_context_bypass` (fast) / local (cheap, via recovery flag)

## Suggested changes and busy-time impact

| Change | Mechanism | Mechanism-based expectation |
|---|---|---|
| Fast COLD 38k → 55k | `new` (full re-prefill) trips less often for 38k–55k sessions | converts part of the 3,773 `large_context_bypass`; +20–40 min compute → +1.5–3 pts busy |
| Fast WARM 100k → ~144k (ratio **and** absolute) | admits 100k–144k contexts | converts part of the 2,200 `context_too_large`; +10–20 min → +1–1.5 pts busy |
| Cheap 3 → 2 slots | physical 83,285 → 100,000 (absolute-bound) | shrinks cheap `context_too_large`; loses one concurrent slot |
| Fast queue depth 3→8 / 45s→120s | converts `fallback_after_queue` (1,871) to local service | +capture, +packing |
| Fast lease 30s → 15s | frees the single fast slot sooner | cuts `local_lease_active`/denials |

**Reconciliation note:** the originating analysis described the second change as "economic ceiling ratio 0.3815 → 0.55 lifts fast warm to ~144k". That is **only true if the absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` is raised in lockstep** (Example 4). The child item must change both values together.

**Guardrails (must stay flat):** p90 TTFT (16.4s total; cheap p90 35.8s already weak), remote-error rate (429 x112), `slot_save failed` (10 — widening the gate admits larger contexts and can increase this), `fallback_after_queue` (must fall), peak concurrency <= slot count (4 = 1+3, at the limit now).

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-14)

Four serial config stages, each followed by its own independent evaluation, then three epic-level traceability/outcome items.

| Order | Item | Purpose | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LP-0MV881O5C007PSL4 | fast queue depth 3->8 / wait 45s->120s | — |
| 1v | LP-0MV881PD50056I57 | evaluate stage 1 | 1 |
| 2 | LP-0MV881OG4003YMM3 | fast idle lease 30s->15s | 1 |
| 2v | LP-0MV881PO8003QAAF | evaluate stage 2 | 2 |
| 3 | LP-0MV881OR2002F26W | fast COLD 38k->55k, WARM 100k->144,179 | 2 |
| 3v | LP-0MV881PZ60030QN3 | evaluate stage 3 | 3 |
| 4 | LP-0MV881P24002187Y | cheap slots 3->2 + warm-cap unlock | 3 |
| 4v | LP-0MV881QA2005MOON | evaluate stage 4 | 4 |
| E1 | LP-0MV8KF7DD004Z7UP | overall busy-time outcome vs 36.5% baseline | 1v..4v |
| E2 | LP-0MV8KF7LW003B2G5 | cross-stage before/after evidence register | 1v..4v |
| E3 | LP-0MV8KF7UG0038YC6 | commit ref + hash traceability | 1..4 |

**Ordering note (test-first exception):** each evaluation item is ordered *after* its target config change because evaluation requires the change to be live, and config changes need a proxy restart (serial experiment). Verification is therefore gated on its stage rather than created ahead of it — a deliberate, documented exception to strict test-first ordering, justified by the A/B nature of the experiment.

**Vertical slice:** each stage cuts end-to-end — config edit, restart/effective-threshold verification, update of any test asserting the changed value, 24h measurement, guardrail check, keep/revert decision. There is no horizontal "all config first" phase.

**Between phases:** before starting the next stage, re-read its item and refresh its baseline/metrics description against the previous evaluation's outcome.

**Plan changelog:**
- 2026-10-14: plan skill run. Children 1–4 (config changes) and 1v–4v (evaluations) already existed from intake; stages 1–4 thresholds re-verified numerically against `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml` and `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`. Auto-coverage had added three epic-level items (E1–E3) as bare AC stubs; their Goal/Method/ACs were fleshed out and dependencies wired (E1/E2 on the four evaluations, E3 on the four config changes). No new substantive features were required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Local busy time (from `proxy-usage-analysis`) is measurably higher than the 36.5% baseline across a comparable 24h window, or the experiment is reverted with recorded evidence.
- [ ] Local capture rate (local served / total demand) is higher than the 14.5% baseline.
- [ ] All guardrail metrics are flat or improved; no critical regression.
- [ ] Each stage records its before/after metrics, the log evidence, and an explicit keep/revert decision.
- [ ] Any accepted config change is committed with the work-item reference and the commit hash recorded on the item.

## Notes

- All arithmetic above was verified against the config on 2026-10-14; re-verify if `local_model_ctx_size`, slot counts, or the absolute warm threshold change.

- **LP-0MS0ZLMO0002E69O** – Fix _should_skip_local to use dynamic new-token threshold instead of binary ratio check (completed)
- **LP-0MRE4NBQ5009V5BX** – Add dual-threshold large-context routing bypass (cold-cache + warm-cache) (completed)

## Goal

Raise the fast-mode large-context routing thresholds so the 46.6%-of-fallbacks `large_context_bypass` band (3,773 events, 99.9% fast) and part of the `context_too_large` band are admitted to the single fast slot, increasing local capture and busy time.

## Context (from parent LP-0MV8805WF007LTZA)

Fast profile today (1 slot × 262,144 ctx):
- COLD `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` = **38,000** (economic new-token threshold; skip reason `large_context_bypass` when a full re-prefill looks expensive) — NOTE: fast does NOT set `local_large_context_economic_bypass_serves_local`, so economic bypasses fall back to remote.
- WARM = `min(physical 258,048, economic)`, economic = `min(round(0.3815 × 262144) = 100,008, absolute 100,000)` = **100,000** (skip reason `context_too_large`).

Worked examples are in the parent item (Examples 1–6, 8). Key messages:

1. **The cold threshold is the binding fast-mode constraint.** Sessions with `est` in (38k, 100k] and a cold cache (cached_ratio ≈ 0, e.g. after the 01:00/10:00 restart) hit `large_context_bypass` at the full prefill cost. Raising COLD moves that band to local unconditionally.
2. **Raising the ratio alone is INERT** — the absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 100000` caps the economic term (Example 4: ratio 0.45 → 117,965 → min(117,965, 100,000) = 100,000; ratio 0.55 → 144,179 → 100,000). WARM must be raised by raising **both** the ratio and the absolute cap.

## Change

`proxy/config-fast.yaml` (overlay):

```yaml
server:
  local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold: 55000
  local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio: 0.55
  local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 144179
```

Resulting fast thresholds (verified arithmetic): physical = 258,048; economic = min(round(0.55 × 262144) = 144,179, 144,179) = 144,179; effective WARM = **144,179**; COLD = **55,000**. The (55k, 144k] band stays non-empty (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP constraint).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `proxy/config-fast.yaml` updated with the three values in the worktree (build → test → commit order); update the golden fixtures and any tests asserting the fast profile thresholds. Verified assertion surface (2026-10-15, repo scan of `config-fast` / `cold_cache_threshold` / `economic_ceiling_ratio` / `warm_cache_threshold` in proxy/tests):
  - `test_economic_ceiling.py::TestShippedConfigDerivesExpectedValues::test_fast_profile_effective_warm` — asserts fast cold 38000 / warm 100000 → update to 55000 / 144179.
  - `test_ctx_slot_validation.py::test_fast_mode_cold_below_warm` — asserts fast cold 38000 / warm 100000 → update to 55000 / 144179.
  - `test_mode_config.py` (~:359) — asserts `fast cold_cache_threshold == 38000` → 55000; (~:360) cheap/fast warm threshold equality breaks once fast sets warm 144179 — both lines (and the equality premise round :360) need updating.
  - `test_config_merge.py::TestDeduplicatedModeFiles::test_residue_server_keys` — fast overlay server-key set must gain the three new keys; the golden fixtures `proxy/tests/fixtures/merged_config_fast.json` and `prededup_raw_fast.json` move cold 38000→55000, ratio 0.3815→0.55, warm 100000→144179 (see Stage 2's lockstep pattern, LP-0MV881OG4003YMM3).
- [ ] Post-restart fast-mode log shows `context_too_large` only above ~144k and `large_context_bypass` shrinking vs the 3,773-event baseline.
- [ ] Local requests / busy time rise measurably over the post-change window (proxy-usage-analysis report) with no critical regression in p90 TTFT (baseline total 16.4s / fast 10.1s), `slot_save failed` (baseline 10 — larger admitted contexts raise ReadTimeout risk), or remote-error rate.
- [ ] The physical clamp still protects: no `finish_reason=length` / KV-overflow 400s from local llama-server at decode time (the F2/F3 undercount caveat, LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM — the `code` alias uses the native Qwen3 tokenizer so its estimates are exact; plan/author use cl100k which undercounts ~1.69x dense-prose tokens: verify no overflow fallbacks appear in the window).
- [ ] Keep/revert decision recorded with evidence.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config-fast.yaml` — overlay updated with the three values (the change).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — base config (unchanged; base keeps ratio 0.3815 / warm 100000 / cold 38000 — verify with `test_base_config_declares_ratio` in test_economic_ceiling.py).
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/merged_config_fast.json`, `proxy/tests/fixtures/prededup_raw_fast.json` — fast golden fixtures updated in lockstep (same pattern as Stage 2 LP-0MV881OG4003YMM3).
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`, `proxy/tests/test_economic_ceiling.py`, `proxy/tests/test_ctx_slot_validation.py`, `proxy/tests/test_mode_config.py` — tests asserting fast profile thresholds (see AC1).

## Risks

- Admitting 100k–144k contexts to the single fast slot risks long prefills (≈70 tok/s prompt eval → tens of seconds to minutes of prefill) and correlates with the `slot_save failed` ReadTimeouts. This is why the change is fast-only and evaluated separately.
- COLD must stay strictly below WARM or the ratio check becomes dead code (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-15: plan skill run (auto-complete, effort Extra Small / risk Low below threshold). Description reviewed by the six automated stages. Changes: AC1 now lists the exact verified test/fixture assertion surface for the fast thresholds; added `## Key Files`. No decomposition required — leaf task with measurable ACs and a minimal implementation sketch. ## Goal

Reduce cheap-mode `context_too_large` fallbacks (2,200 events in window, 71% cheap; cheap skip share 100%) by raising the cheap effective warm threshold via a slot-count change, increasing cheap-mode local capture and busy time (cheap busy baseline 53.7%).

## Context (from parent LP-0MV8805WF007LTZA)

Cheap profile today (3 slots × 262,144 ctx):
- Physical per-slot clamp = `262144 // 3 - 4096` = **83,285** — this is the binding term today (economic = 100,000 > 83,285), so effective WARM = 83,285. COLD = 42,000. `local_large_context_economic_bypass_serves_local: true` (economic bypasses already stay local).
- `context_too_large` fires above 83,285 — anything with est > ~83k goes remote regardless of cache, even though cheap runs `serves_local`.

## Change

`proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (overlay):

```yaml
server:
  session_slot_pool_size: 2
```

**But** (verified arithmetic, Example 7): physical becomes `262144 // 2 - 4096 = 126,976`, and effective WARM = `min(physical 126,976, economic min(100,008, 100,000))` = **100,000** — the **absolute** `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 100000` now binds, so WARM only rises to 100,000, not 126,976. **To unlock the full 126,976 the cheap overlay must also raise the absolute warm cap and ratio** (same lock-step as Stage 3):

```yaml
server:
  session_slot_pool_size: 2
  local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 126976
  local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio: 0.55
```

→ economic = min(round(0.55 × 262144) = 144,179, 126,976) = 126,976 → effective WARM = **126,976**, COLD stays 42,000 (band non-empty).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` updated (slots 3→2, and either the three-value version or the minimum two-value version) in the worktree (build → test → commit order); update tests asserting cheap slot count (search `session_slot_pool_size` in proxy/tests); keep llama-server `--parallel` aligned with `session_slot_pool_size` (lifecycle sets LLAMA_PARALLEL from it — verify at the next cheap-mode restart).
- [ ] Cheap `context_too_large` falls vs the 871-cheap-event baseline; more cheap traffic admitted (Local requests / busy time rise in cheap hours, 01:00–10:00).
- [ ] Guardrails: cheap-mode p90 TTFT (baseline 35.8s — already the weak spot; fewer slots + longer prefills can worsen it), cheap contention events (queue depth 8 / 120s now handles 2-slot bursts), `slot_save failed` (10 baseline).
- [ ] Keep/revert decision recorded with evidence, including whether the modest 100,000 cap (minimum change) or the full 126,976 (three-value change) is retained.

## Risks

- Losing a concurrent cheap slot raises contention sensitivity in the 01:00–10:00 window; the contention queue is the shock absorber.
- Larger admitted contexts couple with the same prefill/slot-save pressure as Stage 3.

## Goal

Determine how often the llama-proxy flips between **fast** and **cheap** modes,
what triggers each flip (in particular the ContextHub/herdr code that initiates
the switch to fast), whether the flip rate is problematic, and what (if
anything) should change to reduce it.

## Context / findings so far

Investigation of the 24h window 2026-10-14 14:02 → 2026-10-15 14:02 UTC found
**30 proxy restarts**, of which **15 were "Mode-switch restart spawned"**
(one restart per real mode transition).

Trigger sources identified:

- **ContextHub / herdr** — `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`:
  - *Fast on command*: records operator activity and fire-and-forget
    `POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`.
  - *Cheap on idle*: leader-only, when idle ≥
    `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (900_000 ms = 15 min) **and** the
    proxy reports idle, gated by the model-cooldown signal.
  - Shared activity broadcast via `mode-activity.json`; leader elected via the
    downtime worker; fail-closed everywhere.
- **Proxy's built-in time schedule** — `proxy/mode_schedule.yaml`
  (cheap 01:00, fast 10:00) = 2/day.
- **Manual** `POST /admin/set-mode` (operators/agents).

Each real transition persists the mode and spawns
`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` (`proxy/proxy/mode.py` `set_mode()` →
`_spawn_restart()`), because fast/cheap are separate config profiles
(`config-fast.yaml` vs `config-cheap.yaml`) with different slot-pool sizes
(fast: base `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; cheap: 3). The restart re-inits
llama-server and typically yields a ~60s local-qwen3 cooldown on a cold-start
503. Redundant switches are skipped (mode already matches), so transition count
== restart-contribution count.

**Is this period unusual?** Historical per-calendar-day mode-switch counts from
the rotated logs: 10-08=28, 10-09=22, 10-10=16, 10-11=10, 10-12=32, 10-13=24,
10-14=31, 10-15=19 (partial, ~14h). So flipping is **endemic (~10–34/day)** —
to be confirmed and extended in this investigation.

## Questions to answer

1. How many flips/day, split by trigger source (ContextHub fast-on-command,
   ContextHub idle-cheap, proxy schedule, manual)?
2. Is the fast-on-command path firing repeatedly during active periods
   (flip-flop)? Quantify fast→cheap→fast pairs within short windows.
3. What is the cost per flip (restart duration, local cooldown, dropped or
   retried in-flight work, cold-prefill thunder)?
4. What else (besides mode) causes the proxy to restart, and how much of the
   flip rate is attributable to each?
5. What options exist to reduce flipping (e.g. minimum-dwell/hysteresis, keep
   fast during working hours rather than idle-cheap, only switch when the
   benefit is real, coalesce/defer switches, non-destructive switch), with
   trade-offs?
6. Recommendation: act or not, and if so, what and with what measurable target?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Flip frequency over ≥7 days of logs is documented (per-day counts +
      intra-day distribution), separated by trigger source.
- [ ] The ContextHub `mode-switch-worker.ts` switching logic is documented
      (triggers, gates, thresholds, leader election, cooldown gate, fail-closed
      behaviour).
- [ ] A quantified answer to "was the studied 24h period unusual?" against the
      ≥7-day baseline.
- [ ] A cost-per-flip estimate (restart duration, local cooldown, in-flight
      impact, cold-prefill effect).
- [ ] A prioritised list of reduction options with expected effect and
      trade-offs, and at least one recommended option with a measurable target.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation work items are created for the recommended
      option(s), or a decision not to act is recorded.
- [ ] Evidence is command/log based and reproducible (exact greps/scripts
      recorded in this item).

## References

- Related items: LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX (time-based schedule),
  LP-0MSMF5LXO006YDNM (in-flight sessions across mode switches),
  LP-0MSMFQ3DL006EY2H (grandfathered routing tests).
- Code: `proxy/proxy/mode.py`, `proxy/mode_schedule.yaml`,
  `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`.
- Logs: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`.

Switching between **fast** and **cheap** modes currently restarts the whole
proxy **and** llama-server, because the two profiles differ in
`session_slot_pool_size` (fast/base = 1, cheap = 3). The restart discards the
warm KV cache and kills in-flight local streams. We need to know whether a
single slot count is viable for both modes — which would let a switch keep the
running llama-server (via the existing adopt/reuse path) — or whether the
per-mode slot count must stay and the already-implemented drain remains the
mitigation.

## Users

- **Agent operators / users** — long-running Pi sessions through the proxy; a
  mode switch today interrupts work and loses the warm cache, degrading the
  next requests' TTFT.
- **Proxy operators** — switch modes manually (UI/API) or on schedule
  (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00) and want the switch to be cheap and
  non-disruptive.
- **Benchmark / maintainer** — needs reproducible numbers to justify (or
  reject) a config change.

User stories:

- As an agent operator, I want a mode switch to preserve the warm local KV
  cache so my next request is not slowed by a cold restart.
- As a proxy operator, I want an evidence-based decision on whether fast and
  cheap can share one slot count, so the restart-on-switch can be removed (or
  knowingly retained).
- As a maintainer, I want the 1/2/3-slot trade-off quantified (per-slot
  context, memory, decode speed, contention) for the small-request workload the
  local slot actually serves.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Benchmark results for 1, 2 and 3 slots are recorded with reproducible
   commands, configs and raw numbers, covering throughput, latency/TTFT,
   queue-timeout / `fallback_after_queue` rate, local stream share, and local
   quarantine episodes, at ≥ the observed concurrency (2–3 concurrent sessions
   plus queue depth).
2. A recommendation states whether a single slot count is viable for both
   modes, the chosen N, and the measured trade-offs (per-slot context, memory,
   decode speed, contention including queue-timeout rate).
3. The evaluation explicitly accounts for large-context bypass traffic
   (400–750/day, `large_context_bypass` / `context_too_large`) when interpreting
   the per-slot context trade-off — i.e. how much of the local-eligible traffic
   is small, and what per-slot context can be given up at higher N.
4. If a single slot count is viable: a follow-up work item is created to
   converge `session_slot_pool_size` across
   `config.yaml` / `config-fast.yaml` / `config-cheap.yaml` and make the switch
   non-destructive by reusing the running llama-server (existing adopt path,
   LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN) rather than restarting it.
5. If not viable: the recommendation documents why, confirms the
   already-implemented bounded drain (`server.mode_switch_drain`,
   LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE) remains the mitigation, and files any gaps found as
   follow-up items (`discovered-from:LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5`).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- The proxy serves concurrent production consumers; the benchmark must not
  permanently destabilise the running config. Any config edit during
  benchmarking must be reverted/restored, and the proxy left in the correct
  scheduled mode.
- Slot count must match llama-server `--parallel`; changing it requires a
  llama-server restart (the very cost under evaluation).
- fast = 1 slot × 262144 ctx; cheap = 3 slots × 262144 ctx. Per-slot context at
  N slots is roughly `ctx_size // N` minus output headroom (routing thresholds
  are auto-derived; see config comments).
- Benchmark scripts/artifacts live under `proxy/benchmarks/`; transient outputs
  must not leave tracked paths permanently dirty.

## Existing state

- `proxy/config.yaml` (base profile) `session_slot_pool_size: 1`;
  `proxy/config-fast.yaml` overrides other values but inherits 1;
  `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` sets `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- A mode switch is a full restart (`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`)
  driven by `proxy/proxy/mode.py`; it also restarts llama-server, so the warm
  KV cache is lost.
- A **bounded drain already exists** (`mode.py`: `_begin_drain`, `draining()`,
  `drain_retry_after()`, `_count_in_flight_local_streams()`,
  `_wait_for_in_flight_local_streams()`, `_spawn_restart`), implemented under
  LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE (completed) and covered by
  `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py`. It defers new chat requests
  (503 + Retry-After) and waits up to `mode_switch_drain.max_seconds`
  (fast 30s, cheap/base 90s). ⇒ the item's conditional "implement a drain"
  branch is already satisfied.
- llama-server reuse/adopt across a proxy-only restart exists in
  `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN), with
  `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` `merged_config_sha256` guarding against
  adopting a stale config.
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD) varies
  1/2/4/6/8/12 slots and measures throughput/latency/TTFT/GPU memory. It does
  **not** currently report queue-timeout rate, local stream share, or
  quarantine episodes, and uses 6 concurrent requests — it may need extension
  for the concurrency/metrics this item requires.
- Contention evidence carried in the item: fast 1-slot 10:00–14:02 window →
  173 `fallback_after_queue`; cheap 3-slot 01:00–10:00 → 207 over a longer
  window; 39 `empty_response` cooldowns cluster under 1-slot contention.

## Desired change

Produce an evidence-backed verdict on a single slot count for both modes and
act on it:

- **Viable** → create a follow-up item to converge the configs and keep
  llama-server warm across the switch (adopt path); the mode switch becomes a
  proxy-only restart.
- **Not viable** → document why and keep the existing bounded drain; file any
  gaps as `discovered-from` follow-ups.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — base profile; `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; routing and
  context thresholds.
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml` — fast overlay; inherits slot count, sets
  `mode_switch_drain.max_seconds: 30`.
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — cheap overlay; `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — existing slot sweep; candidate to
  extend with queue-timeout / local-share / quarantine metrics.
- `proxy/proxy/mode.py` — mode switch, bounded drain, `_spawn_restart`.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — llama-server reuse/adopt across proxy restart
  (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `deep_merge` + `merged_config_sha256`
  stale-adopt guard.
- `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py` — existing drain test coverage.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` — existing benchmark unit tests.

## Related work

- LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD — Slot-count benchmark: optimal `session_slot_pool_size`
  (completed; script reusable).
- LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE — Drain or re-route in-flight local streams at
  mode-switch restart (completed; drain implemented).
- LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H — Stream finish errors: recover-first reroute (completed;
  classified 4 restart-kill events).
- LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN — llama-server reuse across proxy-only restarts (adopt).
- LP-0MRW0WTOO002GG8I — pool 2 → 6 (completed).
- LP-0MQMH0WHY005UPFA — align pool with llama-server `--parallel`.
- LP-0MRDE669Y003V1SO — cache-cold after restart.
- LP-0MSM3TGO3007QN9M — mode control UI.
- LP-0MSMF5LXO006YDNM — in-flight sessions keep their models across mode
  switches (completed).
- LP-0MU5BOK3P0090O0V — mode flapping / switch restarts (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the benchmark can be run without permanently disrupting
  production; the config is restored and the proxy left in the correct
  scheduled mode afterwards.
- **Assumption:** the already-implemented bounded drain satisfies the item's
  conditional "if not viable: implement a drain" branch (see Existing state),
  so the remaining scope is evaluation → recommendation → follow-up items.
- **Risk:** benchmarking 3 × 262144 ctx may OOM or force a lower per-slot
  context, biasing results. Record memory and per-slot context, and treat
  OOM / severely reduced per-slot context as a viability failure.
- **Risk:** the benchmark workload may not match real traffic — large-context
  bypass dominates request counts but never touches the local slot. Characterise
  the local-eligible request mix explicitly.
- **Risk (scope creep):** tuning the drain, changing remote fallback policy, or
  UI changes are **out of scope** here — record as linked follow-up items
  rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (prior mode-flip
investigation) plus repository inspection (`mode.py`, `lifecycle.py`,
`config*.yaml`, `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`) sufficed to draft the
brief. One interpretation was recorded as a documented assumption (see Risks &

# Implement grace-period immunity: local cold-start 503s must not trigger a 60s local cooldown

## Problem statement

After a proxy restart, local (Qwen3) requests that race llama-server warm-up receive HTTP 503 and are treated identically to genuine failures — applying the standard `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` quarantine and feeding the failure counter. This causes the dominant source of ~60s local quarantines (~12 of 45 episodes in one 24h window), even though the 503 reflects "not ready yet" rather than a provider fault.

## Users

- **Local-proxy operator:** wants the proxy to recover immediately after a restart without wasting up to 60s of requests per restart.
- **Pi-extension / end-user:** experiences dropped requests or latency spikes during restarts.

## User stories

- As a proxy operator, when llama-server is cold after a restart, a local request that receives HTTP 503 should defer (Retry-After) without quarantining the provider.
- As a proxy operator, when local continues to return HTTP 503 **after** the warm-up window, the standard cooldown should still apply (genuine faults not masked).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A deterministic unit test reproduces the current cold-start 503 → 60s cooldown, then verifies it no longer occurs after the change.
2. Tests cover:
   - (a) Cold-start 503 within the `is_cold()` warm-up window → defer via Retry-After, no cooldown, no failure-counter bump.
   - (b) Sustained HTTP 503 **after** the warm-up window ends → normal cooldown applies.
   - (c) Connection error during warm-up → defer, no cooldown.
   - (d) Concurrent cold-start dispatch gating (`local_cold_start_max_concurrent`) still respected.
   - (e) A fresh warm-up window begins after each restart (new `note_model_loaded()` arms it).
3. The exponential-backoff failure counter is not polluted during the warm-up window.
4. No regression in routing/fallback tests; full suite passes via `/skill:test` before commit.
5. Follows the implement workflow (worktree, build → test → commit).
6. Logs/metrics evidence pre/post: local cooldown episodes in the hour after a restart drop to ~0.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments in `cold_start.py`/`provider.py`, `proxy/config.yaml` knobs, and any relevant docs entries (e.g. `proxy/docs/`).

## Constraints

- **Reuse `cold_start.is_cold()` as the single immunity-boundary signal.** No new window plumbing. The existing grace window already bounds the immunity period and is self-expiring.
- **Only HTTP 503 + connection errors defer during the window.** All other 5xx during warm-up still quarantine — a genuine sustained non-503 fault is still quarantined.
- **Behaviour applies per restart event.** A new `note_model_loaded()` call arms a fresh warm-up window.
- **Must interact correctly with existing concurrent cold-start dispatch gating** (`local_cold_start_max_concurrent`).
- **No magic sleeps.** The readiness/warm-up signal is explicit and bounded.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: masking genuine local faults.** Mitigated by deferring only HTTP 503 + connection errors, and only while `is_cold()` is True — any other 5xx or post-window 503 still quarantines.
- **Risk: window not armed when 503s arrive.** If some warm-up 503s occur before `note_model_loaded()` arms the window, immunity will not cover them; verifiable in tests/logs, and if a gap exists it becomes a follow-up (not in scope here).
- **Risk: deferral storm.** Deferring during cold-start must respect the existing `local_cold_start_max_concurrent` gating so a burst of deferred requests does not accumulate unboundedly.
- **Assumption:** `is_cold()` semantics (armed at model load, self-expiring grace window) are the correct boundary; per Q1 this was confirmed by the operator.
- **Scope creep guard:** extending immunity to other status codes, other providers, or re-architecting the cold-start state machine is **out of scope** — record as separate work items if discovered.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — manages a bounded cold-start grace window: `note_model_loaded()`, `mark_warm()`, `is_cold()`, `note_backend_down()`. Config: `local_cold_start_grace_seconds` (default 120), `local_cold_start_max_concurrent` (default 1), `local_cold_start_retry_after_seconds` (default 15).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` (line ~4871) calls `mark_provider_unavailable()` for all HTTP errors including 503; `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()` (line ~4832) does the same for connection errors. Exponential backoff only applies to remote providers.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — denies concurrent local dispatches during cold (`is_cold()` check), logs `local_dispatch_denied ... cold_start=True`.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` (line 581).

## Desired change

- In `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` and `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()`, check `cold_start.is_cold(config)`. If cold and the error is HTTP 503 or a connection error, **do not** call `mark_provider_unavailable()` or bump the failure counter. Instead, defer the request (return Retry-After using `cold_start.retry_after_seconds(config)`), and set an appropriate fallback reason.
- The deferred request should behave like a `Retry-After` signal to the caller (existing mechanism already supports this).
- A non-503 HTTP error (e.g., 500, 502) during the window should still call `mark_provider_unavailable()` to avoid masking genuine faults.
- A non-connection error during the window still quarantines normally.

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — read `is_cold()`, `retry_after_seconds()` for immunity decision.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` (~4871), `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()` (~4832), `mark_provider_unavailable()` (~2141).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — cold-start dispatch gating (line ~1086) — verify no interaction conflicts.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `note_model_loaded()` call sites (~230, ~2007, ~2042, ~2222) — confirm window is armed before first 503s.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — cold-start config knobs.
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — existing cold-start admission test suite; add the grace-period immunity cases here (or a sibling test module).
- `proxy/README.md` — update cooldown/cold-start documentation.

## Related work

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR01SJBP005I0OR** — "Fallback not recovering after model-loading 503; returns all providers exhausted" (completed). Sibling investigation.
- **LP-0MUCEEZ6B003NZH5** — "Restart-resilient local dispatch: prevent post-restart pool wedge from no-progress prefills" (completed). Parent epic / adjacent.
- **LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178** — "proxyctl: restart command" (completed). Restart tooling context.
- **LP-0MRE4NBQ5009V5BX** — "Add dual-threshold large-context routing bypass (cold-cache + warm-cache)" (completed). Cold/warm routing interaction.
- **LP-0MUYN2RD800889S2** — "[test-failure] tests/test_cold_start_admission.py::test_proxy_to_local_warm_bypasses_cold_cap — failing test" (completed). Existing cold-start admission test suite.

### Investigation context
- **LP-0MV9UNE75004903J** — mode-flip frequency investigation (restart-frequency context).
- **LP-0MV9UNKVK007TN7E** — proxy restart frequency examination (restart causes).

### Repository references
- `proxy/README.md` — cold-start / cooldown documentation surface.
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — existing cold-start admission tests (extend for immunity cases).

## Appendix

- Q: Where should the immunity window anchor? — Answer (Map): Reuse `cold_start.is_cold()` as the single immunity-boundary signal (recommended option a).
- Q: Scope of deferred failures during the window? — Answer (Map): Strictly HTTP 503 + connection errors; all other 5xx still quarantine (recommended option a).

## Goal

Examine the llama-proxy restart rate: is ~24–34 full proxy restarts/day normal,
what causes each restart, which causes are avoidable, and which should be
fixed.

## Context / findings so far

- Studied 24h window (2026-10-14 14:02 → 2026-10-15 14:02 UTC): **30 full proxy
  restarts** ("Starting LLama Proxy Server"), of which **15 were mode-switch
  restarts** and the rest from other causes.
- Historical per-calendar-day restart counts (rotated logs identified by the
  same marker): 10-08=28, 10-09=22, 10-10=16, 10-11=10, 10-12=32, 10-13=24,
  10-14=34, 10-15=19 (partial, ~14h). So the rate is high but **consistent** —
  likely not unusual for this deployment, to be confirmed and explained.
- Non-mode-switch causes observed (to classify rigorously): llama-server death /
  self-heal ("llama-server process died, restarting..."), TTS watchdog events
  (note: TTS self-heal restarts only the TTS process, `backends/tts.py`
  `_attempt_tts_self_heal`; a full proxy start shortly after a TTS event needs
  explanation), operator-triggered restarts, log/rotation-driven signals.

## Questions to answer

1. What is the distribution of restart causes over ≥7 days (mode-switch,
   llama-server death/self-heal, TTS-watchdog-adjacent, manual/operator,
   crash)?
2. Is the restart rate unusual vs the historical baseline? (Preliminary: no.)
3. Which causes are avoidable (fixable) vs necessary?
4. Does restart churn correlate with local-qwen3 cooldown episodes and remote
   fallback spikes? (Preliminary: yes — 12/45 quarantine episodes followed a
   restart within 75s.)
5. What is the blast radius of a restart (restart duration, cold-prefill,
   in-flight work lost)?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restart causes are classified over ≥7 days with per-cause counts and at
      least one concrete log signature per class.
- [ ] A clear verdict on whether the studied period's restart rate is unusual.
- [ ] Avoidable vs necessary causes are separated, with a prioritised list of
      fixes (e.g. llama-server death root-cause, TTS exit-code=0 investigation,
      non-destructive mode switch).
- [ ] Any fixable cause has a follow-up work item created (or a decision not to
      act recorded).
- [ ] Evidence is reproducible (exact commands/log greps recorded in this
      item).

## References

- Related items: LP-0MRT928DD008136S (TTS watchdog loop),
  LP-0MS0Z9DTA003P6GB (TTS recovery state after llama restart),
  LP-0MS6OY4AA009O78D (restart reliability integration tests),
  LP-0MS6OYDKX004PT0U (fresh HTTP client after llama restart),
  LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178 (proxyctl restart), plus the sibling investigations for
  mode-flip frequency and cold-start grace period.
- Logs: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`.


---

## Resolution (Map, 2026-10-16)

Investigation complete. Full report:
`docs/restart-frequency-analysis-LP-0MV9UNKVK007TN7E.md`.

### Acceptance criteria — met

- [x] **Restart causes classified over ≥7 days with per-cause counts and ≥1 log
      signature per class.** 170 restarts over 2026-10-09 06:06 → 2026-10-16 09:24 UTC
      classified: mode_switch 167 (98.2 %), TTS-watchdog-adjacent 2, unattributed 1,
      independent llama-server death 0. Signatures: `Mode-switch restart spawned`,
      `TTS watchdog: TTS server exited with code=0`, none.
- [x] **Clear verdict on whether the period's rate is unusual.** Not unusual —
      23.8/day is within the historical 10–34/day band; structurally activity-gated.
- [x] **Avoidable vs necessary separated, with a prioritised fix list.** Almost all
      avoidable via a non-destructive mode switch (tracked LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5);
      flip-rate reduction (LP-0MV9UNE75004903J); only the ~10 scheduled transitions/week
      are intended.
- [x] **Any fixable cause has a follow-up item or a recorded decision.** Created
      LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH (restart attributability logging); decisions recorded for the
      remainder (primary fix already tracked by LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 and
      LP-0MV9UNE75004903J; TTS exit-code=0 is a restart artefact, no new TTS item).
- [x] **Evidence reproducible.** Exact `zgrep` commands recorded in the report and in
      the work-item comment.
